sentences.en: Hey guys, it's Joel, and you're listening to the Taproot Therapy Collective PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是Joel，你们正在收听的是Taproot Therapy Collective播客。

sentences.en: Today's article is about the birth of architecture.
sentences.zh: 今天这篇文章的主题是建筑的诞生。

sentences.en: So I was recently in Spain, I put off travel, like the plague.
sentences.zh: 我最近去了趟西班牙，我以前总是像躲瘟疫一样推迟旅行。

sentences.en: Well, not really travel, but vacation time, because I kind of like what I do.
sentences.zh: 其实也不完全是旅行，主要是休假，因为我挺喜欢我现在做的工作。

sentences.en: And it's also more work to leave and come back than it is to not leave.
sentences.zh: 而且离开再回来，比不离开要麻烦得多。

sentences.en: So I don't leave much, and this was like a trip that had been kicked down the road four years due to two COVIDs and health care emergencies and different things.
sentences.zh: 所以我很少出门，这次旅行是因为两次新冠疫情、医疗紧急状况等各种原因，被推迟了四年的行程。

sentences.en: So we kind of had to do it or lose it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们这次不得不去，不然就没机会了。

sentences.en: And when I was in Spain, I drove out to the Dolman de Manga, which no one else in my party had any interest in seeing, which is a Neolithic Dolman.
sentences.zh: 在西班牙的时候，我开车去了曼加石棚墓（Dolman de Manga），那是新石器时代的石棚墓，我同行的其他人对此毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: And I took my daughter, and so I was thinking about that.
sentences.zh: 我带上了我女儿，所以我一直在思考这件事。

sentences.en: I was going to talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我本来打算聊聊这个。

sentences.en: My daughter, Violet, is one of my favorite things.
sentences.zh: 我女儿Violet是我最珍视的人之一。

sentences.en: She really loves Adventure Time, which is this TV show that deals a whole lot with, like, fart jokes and then, like, mythology and Western esoteric magic.
sentences.zh: 她非常喜欢《探险活宝》（Adventure Time），这部动画片里既有很多屁话笑话，又涉及神话和西方神秘学魔法。

sentences.en: And if you've got a kid and you've got to get up at, I don't know, like, 5 or 6 in the morning, don't watch Baby Bum.
sentences.zh: 如果你有孩子，而且不得不每天早上五六点起床，千万别看《Baby Bum》。

sentences.en: Watch Adventure Time.
sentences.zh: 去看《探险活宝》。

sentences.en: Like, the baby finger, baby finger, where are you?
sentences.zh: 像什么“手指宝宝，手指宝宝，你在哪里？”这种。

sentences.en: You're not going to get anything out of that but a migraine.
sentences.zh: 除了让你偏头痛，你什么也得不到。

sentences.en: But Adventure Time, which, I don't know, maybe one day I'll write an article about that one because I really love that show.
sentences.zh: 但《探险活宝》——也许哪天我会专门写篇文章聊聊它，因为我真的很喜欢这部剧。

sentences.en: But I wasn't expecting to like it as much as I did, and it's something that we share.
sentences.zh: 我没想到自己会这么喜欢它，这成了我们共同的爱好。

sentences.en: But the Dolman really looked a lot like something out of the show, Adventure Time.
sentences.zh: 那个石棚墓看起来真的很像《探险活宝》里的场景。

sentences.en: You know, Violet loves mythology.
sentences.zh: 你知道，Violet喜欢神话。

sentences.en: She loves creepy tombs.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢阴森的古墓。

sentences.en: She loves the idea of, like, long-dead empires and the Princess Violet stories I tell her at night.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢那种关于早已消亡的帝国的故事，还有我每晚讲给她的“Violet公主”系列故事。

sentences.en: There's always, like, ancient civilizations that are guessing about, you know, what they did or why they did something, but they never quite know.
sentences.zh: 故事里总会有一些古文明，我们猜测他们做了什么或为什么要那样做，但永远无法完全确定。

sentences.en: She's sort of interested in those limits of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 她对这种知识的边界很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And so she thought this thing was really cool because it is a dolman.
sentences.zh: 所以她觉得这个东西很酷，因为它是一个石棚墓。

sentences.en: It is a portal tomb from the megalithic period where people were making giant things out of stone.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨石时代的门户墓，当时的人们用石头建造巨大的建筑。

sentences.en: This one was a lot older than most of the other ones.
sentences.zh: 这个墓比大多数其他的都要古老得多。

sentences.en: Like, I've been to Stonehenge, but other places.
sentences.zh: 我去过巨石阵，也去过其他地方。

sentences.en: And this one was about 6,000 years old, which is kind of, you wouldn't, I guess, or I didn't expect one of the older ones to be bigger.
sentences.zh: 这个墓大约有6000年的历史，你可能不会想到，或者说我没想到，更古老的建筑反而规模更大。

sentences.en: You would think that architecture, you know, would have moved slowly or progressively.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为建筑的发展应该是缓慢或渐进的。

sentences.en: You know, you start out building small things.
sentences.zh: 比如，你先从建造小东西开始。

sentences.en: Maybe there were small things, and we just don't have them.
sentences.zh: 也许当时也有小的，只是我们没发现而已。

sentences.en: But one of the oldest domes that we have, the most impressive, is one of the biggeSt.
sentences.zh: 但我们现存最古老、最令人印象深刻的圆顶建筑，反而是最大的之一。

sentences.en: So that means that the giant, you know, eight, nine-ton rocks that people had to slowly carve out of a mountain
sentences.zh: 这意味着那些巨大的、重达八九吨的岩石，是人们不得不从山上一点点凿出来的。

sentences.en: and then, you know, move somehow without metal tools, without modern ropes.
sentences.zh: 然后在没有金属工具、没有现代绳索的情况下，以某种方式搬运。

sentences.en: They probably had some kind of rope.
sentences.zh: 他们可能确实有某种绳子。

sentences.en: We're pretty wild.
sentences.zh: 这真是太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And so, Violet going into this thing and touching these, you know, giant stones and, like, feeling it was a really neat thing.
sentences.zh: Violet走进这个建筑，触摸那些巨大的石头，感受这一切，这真的很奇妙。

sentences.en: And what is sort of interesting is the Dolman Dominga, it doesn't face the summer solstice like a lot of them do.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，曼加石棚墓并不像许多其他石棚墓那样朝向夏至点。

sentences.en: It faces the winter solstice, and it does that so that it can face this mountain that looks like a face.
sentences.zh: 它朝向冬至点，这样它就能正对着那座看起来像人脸的山。

sentences.en: And it looks a whole lot like a face.
sentences.zh: 那座山看起来真的很像一张脸。

sentences.en: It's not like you kind of have to squint to see it.
sentences.zh: 不是那种需要眯着眼才能看出来的像。

sentences.en: Like, the mountain even has, like, an Adam's apple.
sentences.zh: 那座山甚至还有喉结。

sentences.en: There's a picture of it on the blog if you want to check it out.
sentences.zh: 如果你想看的话，博客上有它的照片。

sentences.en: But it looks like a giant is, like, sleeping underground.
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像一个巨人在地下沉睡。

sentences.en: And it's laying in the ground, which another, that's, like, another thing that you would find out of Adventure Time.
sentences.zh: 它躺在地上，这又是那种你会从《探险活宝》里看到的东西。

sentences.en: And so, you know, the thing about prehistory is we really, we can't know anything about it because it is before written, you know, history is birthed with the invention of writing.
sentences.zh: 关于史前时代，我们真的无法了解任何确切信息，因为那是文字诞生之前的历史，而历史是随着书写的发明才开始的。

sentences.en: And so, before that, there is no writing, at least not writing that we can read.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，没有文字，至少没有我们能读懂的文字。

sentences.en: You know, there probably were picture symbols like other things that were, you know, proto-writing.
sentences.zh: 当然，可能存在过像其他事物那样的图画符号，也就是原始文字。

sentences.en: But not that we have and not that anyone who is a linguist, a modern linguist, would consider a language, really.
sentences.zh: 但我们没有发现，而且现代语言学家也不会真正将其视为一种语言。

sentences.en: And so, a lot of that, you know, everything that we know is just kind of a guess.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们所知道的一切，大多只是一种猜测。

sentences.en: But you could guess that these people who go to Iberia and then stay in Iberia for a really long time, which, like, after having been to Spain, you kind of see why they would stay.
sentences.zh: 但你可以推测，那些来到伊比利亚半岛并长期定居的人——去过西班牙后，你就能理解他们为什么留下来了。

sentences.en: Because, like, everything in Spain was, like, fragrant and edible.
sentences.zh: 因为西班牙的一切都芬芳且可食用。

sentences.en: It was wild.
sentences.zh: 那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Like, you know, there were obviously a lot of olives when they got there, which we think that it probably took them a long time to figure out how to use them.
sentences.zh: 他们到达时那里显然有很多橄榄，我们认为他们可能花了很长时间才弄清楚如何食用它们。

sentences.en: That's probably not why they stayed.
sentences.zh: 这可能不是他们留下的原因。

sentences.en: That was a byproduct of them staying.
sentences.zh: 这只是他们留下来后的副产品。

sentences.en: But I went on a hike to see some other Neolithic writing that was a lot newer.
sentences.zh: 我去徒步旅行看了一些更新的新石器时代文字。

sentences.en: Because a lot of the sites, like, there's no, like, gate or anything.
sentences.zh: 因为很多遗址都没有大门之类的东西。

sentences.en: You just, you find a GPS point, you hike across somebody's land, you go to, like, a cave and you go see it.
sentences.zh: 你只需要找到一个GPS坐标，穿过别人的土地，走到一个洞穴里去看它。

sentences.en: Again, there's a picture of that on the blog.
sentences.zh: 同样，博客上有那张照片。

sentences.en: There's a little guy made out of iron oxide that was inside of a cave that I went into.
sentences.zh: 我走进的那个洞穴里有一个用氧化铁画的小人。

sentences.en: But real small.
sentences.zh: 非常小。

sentences.en: I mean, cave is a general, or cave is generous.
sentences.zh: 我是说，称之为“洞穴”都有点夸张了。

sentences.en: It was more like a hole.
sentences.zh: 那更像是一个洞。

sentences.en: But, like, on the hike, you know, I picked pink pepper berries, which I guess that's not a local thing.
sentences.zh: 但在徒步过程中，我摘了一些粉红胡椒浆果，我想那不是当地特有的。

sentences.en: But there was, like, these just fennel everywhere that just smelled wonderful.
sentences.zh: 但到处都是茴香，闻起来棒极了。

sentences.en: Like, having a steak that night, I put some of the pepper berries in my pocket.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上吃牛排时，我口袋里还装着一些胡椒浆果。

sentences.en: Like, I, on the hike, got some of the wild garlic.
sentences.zh: 徒步时我还采了一些野蒜。

sentences.en: But it probably wasn't wild.
sentences.zh: 但它可能不是野生的。

sentences.en: It probably was growing because there had been a house there, like, you know, 100 years ago or something.
sentences.zh: 它可能是在那儿长出来的，因为一百年前那里可能有一座房子。

sentences.en: I hiked through what was probably a homestead at one point.
sentences.zh: 我穿过的地方曾经很可能是一个家园。

sentences.en: And then, you know, we grilled some of the fennel bulbs, the garlic.
sentences.zh: 然后我们烤了一些茴香球茎和大蒜。

sentences.en: I found wild sage growing.
sentences.zh: 我还发现了野生的鼠尾草。

sentences.en: And it's just, like, a dry climate with just kind of, like, sandy soil that not a ton can grow in.
sentences.zh: 那是一个干燥的气候，土壤沙化，长不出太多东西。

sentences.en: But the stuff that grows, usually you can eat.
sentences.zh: 但长出来的东西通常都能吃。

sentences.en: And you can see really far.
sentences.zh: 而且视野非常开阔。

sentences.en: It's just a nice place.
sentences.zh: 那是个好地方。

sentences.en: You can kind of see why they hung out long enough to figure out something like architecture, which probably took a long time to be able to figure out how to do.
sentences.zh: 你可以理解为什么他们会待得足够久，去琢磨出建筑这种东西，这可能花了很长时间才掌握。

sentences.en: So this tomb, if you're not familiar, dolmens are portal tombs.
sentences.zh: 所以这个墓，如果你不熟悉的话，石棚墓就是一种门户墓。

sentences.en: So what it is is you get these rocks, you know, some of the ones at this settlement.
sentences.zh: 它的构造是这样的：你找来这些石头，比如这个定居点的一些石头。

sentences.en: Like, the biggest capstone, I think, was, like, 180 tons, which is just insane.
sentences.zh: 最大的顶石我想有180吨重，这简直不可思议。

sentences.en: I mean, you're talking about people, you know, chiseling out an ice cream sandwich style.
sentences.zh: 我是说，人们是在像切冰淇淋三明治一样凿石头。

sentences.en: You're just shaped, not style, shaped.
sentences.zh: 是塑形，不是风格，是塑形。

sentences.en: Like, piece of rock, basically, by chiseling everything else away.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是通过凿掉多余的部分来塑造一块岩石。

sentences.en: Like, there's no way to cut it directly out of the mountain.
sentences.zh: 因为没有办法直接从山上把它切下来。

sentences.en: You have to remove the mountain around it.
sentences.zh: 你必须把周围的山体移除。

sentences.en: And then somehow rolling it, carrying it, lifting it up an earthen ramp, you know, digging up these other stones, putting something there.
sentences.zh: 然后以某种方式滚动、搬运、通过土坡抬起它，挖掘其他石头，把东西放好。

sentences.en: And having this, you know, what was probably a pretty sacred space.
sentences.zh: 并拥有这样一个可能非常神圣的空间。

sentences.en: And to say, like, you know, I hear these debates where people are like, are they religious sites or are they, like, holy spaces or were they practically used
sentences.zh: 我听到过这样的争论，人们在争论它们是宗教场所、神圣空间，还是有实际用途的建筑。

sentences.en: or were they used to convey knowledge?
sentences.zh: 或者是用来传授知识的？

sentences.en: And it was like, all of it, all of it.
sentences.zh: 答案是：都是，全都是。

sentences.en: Like, they didn't have disciplines.
sentences.zh: 因为当时还没有学科之分。

sentences.en: They didn't have anything.
sentences.zh: 他们什么都没有。

sentences.en: I mean, the thing that is so interesting to me about the birth of architecture, right, is that, like, when you dig down and you look at that period of history,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，关于建筑的诞生最有趣的一点是，当你深入挖掘并审视那段历史时期时，

sentences.en: it is, like, one of the first biggest technologies, other than maybe language,
sentences.zh: 它是除了语言之外，最早的重大技术之一，

sentences.en: that, like, rends the earth apart and makes us different.
sentences.zh: 它撕裂了大地，让我们变得与众不同。

sentences.en: And nothing can ever be put back the way it was before.
sentences.zh: 从此一切都无法回到过去的样子了。

sentences.en: Because before that, right, before somebody lugged these stones and made these things,
sentences.zh: 因为在那之前，在有人搬运这些石头并建造这些东西之前，

sentences.en: I mean, granted, it took lifetimes to do this, probably.
sentences.zh: 当然，这可能耗费了他们几代人的时间。

sentences.en: It took coordination that no one had ever seen before, that you had classes of people that could chart the sun, that could measure that with little rocks,
sentences.zh: 这需要前所未有的协调能力，需要有能够观测太阳、用小石头进行测量的阶层，

sentences.en: that could convey to the leadership why this was something that would entrench the overall power and progress of mankind, who could coordinate,
sentences.zh: 能够向领导层传达为什么这能巩固人类的整体力量和进步，能够进行协调的人，

sentences.en: who could, you know, feed the people who were doing this instead of hunting or doing anything else.
sentences.zh: 能够供养那些从事这项工作而不是去狩猎或做其他事情的人。

sentences.en: You know, it was hard work in a time where there wasn't a whole lot of surplus anything.
sentences.zh: 在那个几乎没有任何剩余物资的时代，这确实是艰苦的工作。

sentences.en: But, like, once you do that, you know, before that, what humanity is, is nature.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你做到了，在那之前，人类就是自然的一部分。

sentences.en: I mean, they're walking through nature.
sentences.zh: 他们行走在自然之中。

sentences.en: You know, maybe there's wood houses that I prop these things up.
sentences.zh: 也许有木屋支撑着这些东西。

sentences.en: But if there's a mountain there, right, like, it's there.
sentences.zh: 但如果那里有一座山，它就在那里。

sentences.en: And if there's a tree there, it's there.
sentences.zh: 如果那里有一棵树，它就在那里。

sentences.en: And the world is just this natural thing that I'm encountering as a human, that I'm a part of as a human, that I can't really separate myself from, that I can't really control.
sentences.zh: 世界就是我作为一个人类所面对的自然事物，我是其中的一部分，我无法真正将自己从中分离出来，也无法真正控制它。

sentences.en: You know, the homes that are before this are, you know, maybe you dig down a trench, you put wood over it.
sentences.zh: 在那之前的住所，可能只是挖个沟，上面盖点木头。

sentences.en: But this is just such a temporary little change.
sentences.zh: 但这只是一个非常短暂的小改变。

sentences.en: And this is a guess.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个猜测。

sentences.en: I mean, nothing like that would have lasted.
sentences.zh: 因为那样的东西根本保存不下来。

sentences.en: I mean, we have, it does in other parts of Europe.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲其他地方确实有。

sentences.en: So we know that, you know, people were probably doing that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道人们可能确实在那样做。

sentences.en: But, like, and I'm not an archaeologist, you know.
sentences.zh: 但我不是考古学家。

sentences.en: I had a couple of archaeology classes.
sentences.zh: 我只上过几门考古课。

sentences.en: But we come back on the show a ton to the origin, the intersection of, like, psychotic experience, the collective unconscious,
sentences.zh: 但我们在节目中经常回到起源问题，即精神病体验、集体潜意识、

sentences.en: you know, the psychosis and technology and how technological progress changes what we view as human, changes what we view as the world, changes the way that we hallucinate,
sentences.zh: 精神病与技术之间的交集，以及技术进步如何改变我们对人类的看法，改变我们对世界的看法，改变我们产生幻觉的方式，

sentences.en: changes the way that we create and believe, you know, changes religion.
sentences.zh: 改变我们创造和信仰的方式，改变宗教。

sentences.en: And that these things are, like, so, you know, intertwined together in a way that we can see, but we can't directly understand.
sentences.zh: 这些事物以一种我们能看到却无法直接理解的方式交织在一起。

sentences.en: You know, we can only intuitively understand them.
sentences.zh: 我们只能凭直觉去理解它们。

sentences.en: Maybe that's why I like that so much.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是我为什么这么喜欢它的原因。

sentences.en: And when you have somebody who has seen these structures that are basically wood and mud, and the earth is going to reclaim it,
sentences.zh: 当你看到那些基本上是木头和泥土构成的结构，大地终将收回它们时，

sentences.en: yeah, you propped up a lean-to, but you don't really matter.
sentences.zh: 是的，你搭了个棚子，但你并不重要。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, you see in the center of your society that there is a domed thing that can communicate with the heavens,
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，你看到在社会中心出现了一个能与天堂交流的圆顶建筑，

sentences.en: that can predict what the sun is going to do.
sentences.zh: 它能预测太阳的运行。

sentences.en: Because on the day that the sun casts its longest shadow, that shadow reaches all the way through the doorway of this thing that is sort of made to look like nature.
sentences.zh: 因为在太阳投下最长阴影的那一天，阴影会穿过这个看起来像自然景观的建筑的门口。

sentences.en: Like, we couldn't even conceive of a skyscraper or anything that was, like, too different from nature at that point.
sentences.zh: 当时我们甚至无法构想出摩天大楼或任何与自然截然不同的东西。

sentences.en: We had to put earth on either side of these rounded, of these, like, pointed stones with a flat top to make them more natural, to make them more organic,
sentences.zh: 我们必须在这些圆形的、尖锐的石头两侧堆上泥土，并加上平坦的顶部，使它们看起来更自然、更具机体感，
